comparisons.peer_summary: AMD was the first company to integrate a dedicated neural processing unit (NPU) on the same SoC as an x86 CPU for AI PCs.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD identify the integration of a Neural Processing Unit (NPU) as a defining feature of their 2024 client CPU launches for AI PCs. Intel launched the Core Ultra Series 1 as its 'first product with an integrated neural processing unit,' while AMD highlights being 'the first company to integrate a dedicated neural processing unit (NPU) on the same SoC as an x86 CPU for AI PCs.' Both disclosures frame the NNP as a key competitive driver for the emerging AI PC market.

sentences.text: ▪Client CPUs. In 2024, we ramped sales of the Intel® Core™ Ultra Series 1, our first product with an integrated neural processing unit for efficient processing of AI workload. The Intel Core Ultra Series 1, manufactured on the Intel 4 process, introduced the first AI PCs to the market. We also launched the Intel Core Ultra 200V Series, showcasing power efficiency and long-lasting battery life. The 200V Series, manufactured by an external foundry, leverages our Xe2 GPU architecture, bringing improved efficiency, second-generation ray tracing units and XMX AI acceleration to thin and light notebooks. During 2024, a significant majority of our client sales consisted of our 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors, manufactured on Intel 7, which allow us to serve the breadth of customer and computing needs in the client market.
AMD was the first company to integrate a dedicated neural processing unit (NPU) on the same SoC as an x86 CPU for AI PCs.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD offers mobile Ryzen processors with leadership performance and battery life, including the 2024 release of Ryzen AI 300 Series with NPUs and Zen 5 architecture, previous generations with Zen 4/Zen 3+/Zen 2, and Ryzen Z1 Series for handheld gaming.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the specific product series launched in 2024 to address the client/AI PC market. Intel launched the 'Intel Core Ultra 200V Series' and 'Core Ultra Series 1,' while AMD released the 'AMD Ryzen AI 300 Series processors' in 2024. Both disclosures note that these new series leverage advanced architectures (Intel's Xe2 GPU/AI acceleration; AMD's 'Zen 5') to deliver AI capabilities and performance for notebooks.

comparisons.peer_topic: PC Market AI Capabilities and Client SSD Portfolio Expansion
comparisons.peer_summary: Next-generation PCs require higher performance SSDs due to AI capabilities; SBU expanded its portfolio in 2024 with the 3500 NVMe SSD built on Micron G8 NAND, targeting demanding business and consumer workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures link the 2024 product portfolio expansion to the rise of AI capabilities in next-generation PCs. Intel's Core Ultra Series 1 is described as introducing 'the first AI PCs to the market' with AI workloads, while Micron states that 'next generation PCs contain high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI capabilities' and correspondingly expanded its SSD portfolio with the 3500 NVMe SSD to handle these demanding AI workloads.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA RTX enhances gaming with GPU-sophisticated software, ray tracing for cinematic rendering, and DLSS AI technology to boost frame rates.
comparisons.comparison: While Intel focuses on CPU-integrated NPUs for AI PCs, NVIDIA highlights its RTX technology as the leader in the AI PC ecosystem. Intel notes its Core Ultra Series 1 introduced the 'first AI PCs to the market,' whereas NVIDIA states its RTX platforms leverage 'AI technology that boosts frame rates' and positions itself as the 'AI PC leader' with over 100 million AI-capable PCs, indicating a competitive divergence in how they define and lead the AI PC segment (CPU-centric NPU vs. GPU-centric AI acceleration).

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the use of a Neural Processing Unit (NPU) as a critical component for on-device AI inference in their 2024 client computing products. Intel's Core Ultra Series 1 features an 'integrated neural processing unit for efficient processing of AI workload,' and Qualcomm describes its AI Engine as including a dedicated hardware component, the Hexagon NPU, designed for 'sustained, high-performance AI inference' on devices.
